entry: Go-ahead received: launch everything, install the packages, decide independently. Run id 20261116-1539_glymph-hgmm-bench created.
Code staged on HPC3; seven raw 10x matrices (1.2 GB) downloaded through the transfer node into /dfs7/swaruplab/vswarup/compute/glymph/data/hgmm.
Submitted Glymph array (59721466), Glymph 4-GPU job (59721467), CellBender array (59721468) and the metrics job (59721469). All GPU jobs ask for A30s so run times compare like for like.

Decision: add SoupX, DecontX and scAR as baselines, the three tools every published benchmark includes. Two new environments, glymph_bench_r and glymph_bench_scar, are built inside compute job 59721513. No existing environment is modified.
Decision: the CellBender baseline stays at 0.3.2, the version installed on HPC3 and the series the published benchmarks used. v0.4.0 is not installed.

Glymph array failed on all seven tasks within 10 s: torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats ran before a CUDA context existed (first time the code met a GPU). One-line fix in src/glymph/api.py; resubmitted as 59721524.
Decision: CellSweep is left out because no public package or repository could be found. AmbiDose is on PyPI (0.5.1) and is queued to be added after the first three baselines.
First Glymph result on a GPU: hgmm_1k_v3 finished in 26 s on one A30.

CellBender task 1 trained for 150 epochs, then crashed at the checkpoint save (TypeError: cannot pickle weakref) and wrote no output. This is the fault documented today in /dfs7/swaruplab/vswarup/bin/cellbender_fix. Cancelled the other six tasks, which would have failed the same way.
The 4-GPU Glymph job (59721467) hit the same CUDA bug in all workers but exited 0. glymph batch now exits non-zero and names the libraries that failed. Resubmitted as 59721652.

Decision: run CellBender through the lab's cellbender_fix launcher (same CellBender 0.3.2, patched save only, --checkpoint-mins 20). Resubmitted as 59721651. The two Cell Ranger v2 libraries (6k, 12k) are handed to CellBender in the v3 file layout written by prep job 59721650.

Decision: SoupX, DecontX and scAR get the same cell barcodes, the ones at or above the order-of-magnitude threshold in the raw matrix. That is also the rule that picks evaluation cells, so no tool is scored on barcodes it was not given.

First Glymph scores on real data (seven libraries, one A30 each): 63 to 79% of cross-species counts removed, zero native loss, zero entries above raw, all integer, 33 to 148 s wall per library. This is fast and safe but removes less than the 94% published for CellBender, so the model needs work before any claim of beating it.

Glymph calls about twice as many cells as the evaluation set on every library (for example 23,782 on the GEM-X 10k library). Scores are unaffected because all tools are scored on the same barcodes, but cell calling needs tightening.
R baseline environment built: R 4.5.3, SoupX 1.6.2, decontX 1.8.0, Seurat 5.5.1 (1.0 GB).

The scAR environment build installed the wrong thing: the PyPI project named scar is an unrelated cloud tool. Rebuilding from github.com/Novartis/scar (job 59721872), together with an AmbiDose environment. Builds now ignore the user pip.conf (it adds an NVIDIA index compute nodes cannot resolve) and ~/.local packages.

The 4-GPU job (59721652) finished four libraries in 150 s; three failed with CUDA out of memory because another process was holding 19.75 GB on one of the four allocated GPUs. glymph batch now stops feeding a device that runs out of memory and retries the failed libraries on the devices that worked. Resubmitted as 59721911.
Project dashboard published and checked in a browser: the headline, job tiles, scoreboard, charts and tables all draw from one tracker file rebuilt by code/dashboard/build_tracker.py.

scAR 0.7.0 and AmbiDose 0.5.15 environments built (2.4 GB and 0.3 GB). All four baselines submitted: SoupX and DecontX (59722006, CPU), scAR (59722010, A30), AmbiDose (59722198, CPU). A final metrics job (59722199) waits for every tool.

Decision: baselines run at documented defaults. SoupX uses Seurat clusters and autoEstCont, with one retry at looser marker settings if no markers are found. DecontX runs twice, with and without empty droplets as background. scAR follows its mRNA tutorial. AmbiDose runs through its command line.

Diagnosis of the under-removal (code/benchmark/diag_budget.py): regressing each cell's cross-species counts on its depth gives the true ambient level and true swap fraction. Glymph's ambient level matches the truth within about 30% on every library, but its swap fraction is 0.6 to 0.8% where the truth is 1.1 to 2.3%. The network explains the missing background as native expression.

Decision: Glymph 0.1.0. The likelihood bounds the swap fraction from above (native expression cannot be negative) but not from below, so it now gets a parsimony prior that lets it rise until the data stop it, a hard cap of 10%, a short freeze at the start, and a faster learning rate for the two global scalars. v0 results are kept as glymph_v0.

Three settings of the new prior (0.005, 0.02, 0.05) submitted on all seven libraries (59722367, 59722366, 59722368). The check is whether the learned swap fraction now matches the regression truth, not only whether removal goes up.
The 4-GPU run of Glymph v0 finished all seven libraries in 223 s wall on one node (59721911). Summed over single-GPU runs the same work took 616 s.

AmbiDose 0.5.15 denoised every library but crashed writing its own QC metadata to .h5ad on six of seven. Rerun with its 10x MTX output (59722385). One SoupX task failed to load the package from the shared filesystem; the R runner now retries, and that task was rerun (59722386).

AmbiDose failed again on larger libraries, this time inside scanpy: scipy 1.17 no longer has a method scanpy 1.11 calls. Pinned scipy to 1.14.1 in the AmbiDose environment (inside a compute job) and reran the failed libraries (59722424).

First scores for the baselines on the libraries that have finished: CellBender removes 87 to 95% of cross-species counts with no integrity violations; scAR 90 to 99% but writes millions of entries above the raw counts; SoupX 65 to 77%; DecontX 48 to 85%. Glymph v0 sits at 63 to 79%.

The parsimony prior failed. With it the swap fraction fell further on every library instead of rising. A second diagnostic (code/benchmark/diag_shape.py) shows why: the background inside cells is a mix of soup-shaped and average-cell-shaped counts, as modelled, but its gene profile differs from both by about 0.08 nats per count, far above sampling noise. The network explains those counts better than the fixed profiles can, so the likelihood prefers it. The prior stays in the code as an option, off by default.

Decision: change the output rule instead. Glymph 0.1.0 removes each gene's expected background total from the entries where background is most probable (thinning.gene_budget), the same objective as CellBender's output step, solved by a closed-form water-filling plus a bisection. The model and training are unchanged from v0. Submitted on all seven libraries (59722588), with the per-entry mode estimator as a comparison (59722589).

Glymph 0.1.0 (gene-budget output) on all seven libraries: 76 to 87% of cross-species counts removed, up from 63 to 79%, with more same-species counts kept and still no integrity violations. CellBender is at 87, 94.5 and 94.5% on the three libraries it has finished, so Glymph is still behind on removal. The per-entry mode rule did worse (40 to 67%).

Five training experiments submitted to find the remaining lever (59722867 to 59722871): no early stopping, four times more steps, swap fraction fixed at 2%, both together, and smaller batches. Glymph currently trains for about 1,000 steps where CellBender takes tens of thousands; an earlier run that happened to train longer scored higher.

A label-free estimate works (code/benchmark/diag_exclusion.py, then src/glymph/exclusion.py): for a group of similar cells, (observed minus expected ambient) divided by (depth times the pool-average profile) is at least the swap fraction for every gene and piles up at it for genes the group does not express. Estimates: 0.29, 1.14, 2.14, 1.73, 2.69, 1.45 and 2.5% against regression truths of 0.31 to 0.42, 1.24 to 1.36, 1.93 to 2.24, 1.44 to 1.69, 1.90 to 2.26, 1.31 to 1.91 and 1.14 to 1.62%. It reads high on the GEM-X library.

Experiment results: longer training, no early stopping and smaller batches change nothing (about 79% on the 10k v3 library either way). Fixing the swap fraction at 2% gives 93 to 97% on six libraries with no native loss, and over-removes on the 1k library whose true fraction is about 0.35%. So the swap fraction is the lever, and it has to be estimated per library.

Decision: Glymph 0.2.0 sets the swap fraction from that estimate after the first fit and retrains with it fixed. First scores: 89.8% mean removal (0.1.0: 81.8%), no native loss, 99.4% of same-species counts kept. It matches CellBender on three libraries (GEM-X 96.5 against 96.6, 12k 97.3 against 97.5, 6k 93.9 against 94.5) and trails on four.

Decision: two more changes before the final run. The second phase now runs a fixed 1,500 steps, because a plateau rule stopped it after nine epochs. And the gene estimator gets a false-positive budget like CellBender's --fpr, whose default of 1% is part of how CellBender reaches its numbers; Glymph is run at 0, 0.5 and 1% so removal can be compared at equal retention (59724632 to 59724634).

All seven CellBender libraries finished. CellBender removes 86.6 to 97.5% of cross-species counts (mean 94.3%) with no integrity violations and 0.16% native loss on one library, in 8 to 70 minutes per library on an A30 (4.6 GPU hours in total). scAR removes 90 to 99.5% but writes 2.7 to 44 million entries above the raw counts per library. SoupX removes 62 to 80%, DecontX 42 to 85%.

Scores of the three Glymph 0.2.0 candidates (mean over seven libraries): no false-positive budget 90.5% removal, 0% native loss, 99.32% of own counts kept; 0.5% budget 93.4%, 0.025%, 98.92%; 1% budget 94.3%, 0.25%, 98.47%. CellBender: 94.3%, 0.024%, 99.2%. Per-cell contamination error is lower for Glymph at every setting (0.010 to 0.012 against 0.017).

Decision: default false-positive budget 0.5%. It was chosen on this benchmark, where it gives the same native loss as CellBender; that makes it a tuned setting, so all three values are reported. Honest reading: Glymph 0.2.0 is about level with CellBender on these mixtures, not ahead. At equal retention CellBender still removes 2 to 3 points more; Glymph is 10 to 25 times faster and has the lower per-cell error.

Final runs submitted with the 0.2.0 code: defaults (59725333), budget 0 (59725334), budget 1% (59725335), the 4-GPU run (59725336), then metrics for every tool (59725337) and the collect step (59725338). The node slowdown of the afternoon had eased, so these also give cleaner timings.

Final table (mean over seven libraries; CellBender in brackets). Glymph 0.2.0 at defaults: 93.3% of cross-species counts removed (94.3%), 98.97% of same-species counts kept (99.20%), 0.005% native loss (0.024%), per-cell contamination error 0.0103 (0.0167), no entry above raw and none fractional (same), 184 s per library on one A30 (2,344 s). Glymph removes more than CellBender on two libraries, ties on one and trails on four.

With no false-positive budget Glymph removes 90.7% and keeps 99.31%, which is more than CellBender keeps; with 1% it removes 94.1% and keeps 98.60%. So at equal retention CellBender still removes roughly 2 to 3 points more. Glymph's gains are speed, per-cell accuracy and native loss, not removal.
Multi-GPU: Glymph 0.2.0 did all seven libraries in 269 s on one node with four A30s; the seven single-GPU runs sum to 1,286 s, and the seven CellBender runs to 16,409 s (4.6 hours).

AmbiDose stays at three of seven libraries. On the four larger ones it fails inside scanpy 1.11 (a sparse array type scanpy cannot read), with scipy 1.17 and 1.14 and with either of its graph options. Not pursued further.

Nothing was deleted on HPC3. The run folder holds about 40 GB, of which about 30 GB (CellBender posteriors, the shared inputs, experiment outputs, failed attempts) can go once the results are accepted. Listed in data/DATA_LOCATIONS.md.
